record.original_question: Let X be a Fano variety and T_X its tangent sheaf. Give a purely algebraic proof that if X is K-semistable, then T_X is semistable with respect to the polarization -K_X. Also give a purely algebraic proof that if T_X is polystable, then there exists a quasi-etale cover f: Y -> X such that Y decomposes as a product of varieties Y = \prod_i X_i and the pulled-back tangent sheaf T_Y = f^*(T_X) decomposes as a direct sum  igoplus_i T_{X_i}, with each T_{X_i} stable with respect to -K_Y.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Fano variety over $\mathbb{C}$, that is, a normal projective variety with at worst klt singularities such that the anticanonical divisor $-K_X$ is an ample $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier divisor. Let $T_X$ denote the tangent sheaf of $X$. Recall that a torsion-free coherent sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $X$ is slope semistable (resp. stable, polystable) with respect to the polarization $-K_X$ if for every coherent subsheaf $0 \neq \mathcal{G} \subsetneq \mathcal{F}$ of strictly smaller rank one has $\mu_{-K_X}(\mathcal{G}) \le \mu_{-K_X}(\mathcal{F})$ (resp. $<$, resp. semistable and isomorphic to a direct sum of stable subsheaves of equal slope), where $\mu_{-K_X}(\mathcal{F}) = \frac{c_1(\mathcal{F})\cdot (-K_X)^{n-1}}{\mathrm{rank}(\mathcal{F})}$ and $n = \dim X$. A finite surjective morphism $f: Y \to X$ between normal varieties is called quasi-étale if it is étale in codimension one. Prove the following two statements using only algebro-geometric methods (without invoking the existence of Kähler–Einstein metrics or other transcendental/analytic tools):

(1) If $X$ is K-semistable, then $T_X$ is slope semistable with respect to $-K_X$.

(2) If $T_X$ is slope polystable with respect to $-K_X$, then there exists a quasi-étale cover $f: Y \to X$ such that $Y$ admits a decomposition $Y = \prod_i X_i$ as a product of normal projective varieties, the pullback of the tangent sheaf decomposes correspondingly as $f^*(T_X) = T_Y = \bigoplus_i T_{X_i}$ (where each $T_{X_i}$ is identified with its pullback to $Y$), and each summand $T_{X_i}$ is slope stable with respect to $-K_Y$.
artifact.status_search_result: A purely algebraic proof of these statements is explicitly listed as an open problem in the survey on open problems in K-stability of Fano varieties. Analytic proofs via Kähler–Einstein metrics are known (Tian, Donaldson, and others), and partial algebraic results exist for log-Fano pairs and special cases (e.g., logarithmic tangent sheaf semistability), but no fully algebraic proof of (1) and (2) in the general singular Fano setting appears to have been published as of mid-2026.

status_evidence.title: K-stability of Fano varieties: an algebro-geometric approach
status_evidence.snippet: Algebro-geometric approach to K-stability; semistability of tangent sheaves discussed as a consequence of K-semistability via analytic methods.
status_evidence.claim: The implication K-semistable ⇒ T_X semistable is known via analytic (Kähler–Einstein) methods; an algebraic proof remains sought.

status_evidence.title: On the stability of extensions of tangent sheaves on Kähler–Einstein Fano/Calabi–Yau pairs
status_evidence.snippet: The logarithmic tangent sheaf T_S(−log Δ) is slope semistable with respect to −(K_S+Δ) for log-Fano pairs admitting KE metrics.
status_evidence.claim: Partial algebraic/analytic results exist for log-Fano pairs, but a general algebraic proof in the K-semistable setting is not established.
